summary: Humboldt County lookout under construction in 1934 and staffed in 1956 after a gap from 1947; listed as gone, with no removal date or site description found.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Six Rivers National Forest)
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks it removed with no date; firelookout.org lists it as gone

staffing.status: ranger stationed in the 1956 season, described as the first since 1947

events.note: Site being located in March 1934; foundations laid by August 1934; completion date not given
The 1956 item calls the 1956 season the first since 1947, read here as the last staffed season before 1956
A ranger was stationed at the lookout for the season, per a Eureka Humboldt Times item of August 1956

evidence.supports: Blue Lake Advocate item: men stationed there while locating the new lookout station, March 1934
evidence.quote: engaged in locating the new lookout station on Grouse Mountain

evidence.supports: Shasta Courier item: foundations laid and materials hauled, August 1934
evidence.quote: Foundations are being laid for the tower and all material is being hauled to the location

evidence.supports: Shasta Courier item: lower Trinity district to have three lookout towers complete soon, if work kept pace
evidence.quote: the lower Trinity district will soon have three lookout towers complete

evidence.supports: 1956 staffing, first season since 1947, Six Rivers National Forest
evidence.quote: A ranger is stationed in the Grouse Mountain lookout of the Six Rivers National forest for the first season since 1947

evidence.supports: U.S. Forest Service is the reporting agency in the 1956 item
the Forest Lookouts page marks the lookout as removed
firelookout.org index row: Grouse Mountain, Humboldt, tower, gone

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, both thin: one page of 1934 and 1956 newspaper items quoted by Forest Lookouts, and one index row. No removal date, no site description, and no access information. The 'first season since 1947' wording is read as a staffing gap, and the item does not say what the tower was used for in between. Two searches for Six Rivers Forest Service lookout records returned nothing specific. The brief record (tower, gone, Humboldt) matches the index row; no corrections proposed.
